questions.context: Immunity in our body is of two types : (i) Innate immunity and (ii) acquired immunity. Innate immunity is a non-specific defence mechanism, whereas acquired immunity is pathogen-specific; it is called specific immunity too. Acquired immunity is characterised by memory. Antibodies are specific to antigens and there are different types of antibodies produced in our body : they are IgA, IgE, IgG and IgM. It shows primary response when it encounters the pathogen for the first time and secondary response during the subsequent encounters with the same Antigen/Pathogen.

(ii) Mention the number of chromosomes at each stage. Correlate the life phases of the individual with the stages of the process.
questions._drawFigure: (i) a schematic flow of oogenesis: oogonium (2n = 46) dividing by mitosis in the foetal ovary, primary oocyte (2n = 46) arrested in prophase I within the primary follicle (birth to puberty), meiosis I at puberty giving the secondary oocyte (n = 23) and the first polar body in the tertiary/Graafian follicle, the secondary oocyte released at ovulation, and meiosis II (on sperm entry at fertilisation) giving the ovum (n = 23) and the second polar body; each stage labelled with its chromosome number and the life phase.
